original.target_description: MIDUS first two waves, perceived present–future personality similarity predicting life satisfaction 10 years later; Table 2 Model 2, controlling for age, gender, log income, and education.

n.location: p. 3, Table 2, Model 2, Observations row; p. 2, Exclusions and outliers
n.sample_role: Participants with complete covariates in the primary specification and without included continuous-variable outliers; analytic observations shared across Models 1–3.
n.exclusions: Restricted to non-missing values for all covariates in Table 2 Model 3; dropped respondents with any included continuous measure more than 3 SD above or below its mean.

es.metric: standardized regression coefficient (printed b; Table 2 states all variables other than contrast-coded gender are standardized)
es.location: Printed p.3, Table 2, 1995 perceived similarity row, Model (2); table note and Primary Results
es.quote: 1995 perceived similarity ... .163*** [.128, .198] ... All other variables are standardized.

p.location: Printed p.3, Primary Results, Table 2 Model 2
p.quote: After including standard controls ... (i.e., age, gender, income, and education), the coefficient ... remained significant (b ¼ .163, 95% CI ¼ [.128, .198], p < ... .001).

replication.target_description: Study 2, Michigan State University undergraduate cross-sectional sample, perceived similarity predicting concurrent life satisfaction; Table 9 Model 2, controlling for age and gender. The supplied neutral description specifies well-being 10 years later; this study has concurrent well-being.

n.location: p. 798 (PDF p. 8), Table 9, Model 2, Observations row; Analytic Strategy
n.sample_role: Analytic participant observations for the Study 2 regression.
n.exclusions: 1,250 recruited. Authors used original analytic code, additionally excluding participants who reported not answering honestly or not taking participation seriously. Exact counts by exclusion reason are not printed here; four participants did not disclose age.

es.metric: b (standardized; Table 9 states all other variables are standardized)

reported_success.quote: We were able to reproduce and replicate this similarity effect with the original sample and a new sample. [...] However, when using a polynomial regression and response surface approach, a similarity effect between the present and future self did not emerge—neither in the original sample (Study 1) nor in the new sample (Study 2).

notes:
Primary-source titles and DOIs verified in the acquired full texts. Original supplied locator p. 2 describes methods; target statistics are on p. 3, Table 2. Replication supplied locator p. 9 contains discussion/response-surface figure; the difference-score regression is on PDF p. 8, Table 9. Study 2 uses concurrent, adjusted student life-satisfaction items rather than life satisfaction 10 years later; target_match is false for this known outcome/time mismatch. Model 2 replication controls age and gender only, whereas original Model 2 also controls income and education. Replication beta is retained at the .302 precision printed in prose (Table 9 rounds it to .30); p comes from the same regression in Table 9. Success label captures the authors’ replication of the difference-score association and their explicit methodological critique. Quotes normalize PDF extraction artifacts for mathematical symbols and line breaks; bracketed ellipsis separates passages.
